title: Serampore Mission established by Carey, Marshman and Ward
note: William Carey, Joshua Marshman and William Ward set up the Baptist mission at Danish Serampore, which went on to translate and print the Bible in many Indian languages.

title: British and Foreign Bible Society founded
note: The society was formed at the London Tavern to distribute the Scriptures without note or comment, becoming a model for Bible societies worldwide.

title: Battle of Trafalgar
note: A British fleet under Nelson defeated the combined French and Spanish fleets off Cape Trafalgar; Nelson was killed in the action.

title: Adoniram and Ann Judson sail from Salem for Asia
note: Among the first American overseas missionaries, the Judsons left Salem on the brig Caravan; they later served for decades in Burma.

title: Battle of Borodino
note: Napoleon's army and the Russian army under Kutuzov fought the bloodiest single day of the 1812 campaign west of Moscow (26 August Old Style).

title: Battle of Waterloo
note: Allied forces under Wellington and Prussian troops under Blücher defeated Napoleon, ending his final return to power.

title: American Bible Society founded
note: Delegates from local Bible societies met in New York City and formed a national society to publish and distribute the Bible.

title: Stockton and Darlington Railway opens
note: The line opened with George Stephenson's Locomotion No. 1 hauling the first train, the first public railway to use steam locomotives.

title: Slavery Abolition Act takes effect
note: The British act abolishing slavery in most of the Empire, including British North America, came into force.

title: Morse sends "What hath God wrought"
note: Samuel Morse sent the first official long-distance telegraph message from Washington to Baltimore, quoting Numbers 23:23.

title: YMCA founded in London
note: George Williams and fellow drapery workers founded the Young Men's Christian Association for prayer and Bible study.

title: Nova Scotia gains responsible government
note: A new Executive Council answerable to the elected assembly was sworn in, the first responsible government in what is now Canada.

title: Hudson Taylor sails for China
note: James Hudson Taylor left Liverpool aboard the Dumfries on his first voyage to China as a missionary.

title: First Fulton Street noon prayer meeting
note: Jeremiah Lanphier's lunchtime prayer meeting in New York grew into the widespread Prayer Meeting Revival of 1857-58.

title: Tischendorf is shown Codex Sinaiticus
note: On his third visit to St Catherine's Monastery, Constantin von Tischendorf was shown the bulk of the fourth-century Bible manuscript.

title: Darwin's On the Origin of Species published
note: Charles Darwin's book setting out the theory of evolution by natural selection was published in London.

title: Russia's Emancipation Manifesto frees the serfs
note: Tsar Alexander II signed the manifesto and statutes abolishing serfdom (19 February Old Style).

title: Bombardment of Fort Sumter opens the US Civil War
note: Confederate batteries fired on the federal fort in Charleston Harbor, beginning the American Civil War.

title: Charlottetown Conference opens
note: Delegates from the Maritimes and the Province of Canada met to discuss union, a first step toward Confederation.

title: Lee surrenders at Appomattox Court House
note: General Robert E. Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia to Ulysses S. Grant, effectively ending the Civil War.

title: William Booth begins the East London mission
note: Booth's tent meetings in Whitechapel began the Christian Mission, renamed the Salvation Army in 1878.

title: Lammermuir Party sails for China
note: Hudson Taylor and the first large group of China Inland Mission workers sailed from London on the clipper Lammermuir.

title: Canadian Confederation
note: The British North America Act took effect, uniting Nova Scotia, New Brunswick and the Province of Canada as the Dominion of Canada.

title: Golden Spike completes US transcontinental railroad
note: The Central Pacific and Union Pacific lines were joined at Promontory Summit, Utah.

title: Suez Canal opens
note: The canal linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea was formally opened to shipping.

title: Vatican I defines papal infallibility
note: The First Vatican Council approved the constitution Pastor aeternus on papal primacy and infallibility.

title: Wreck of the SS Atlantic off Nova Scotia
note: The White Star liner struck rocks near Terence Bay in the early hours, with heavy loss of life; local residents rescued many survivors.

title: Bell makes the first telephone call
note: Alexander Graham Bell spoke to his assistant Thomas Watson over his new instrument in Boston.

title: Climactic eruption of Krakatoa
note: A series of colossal explosions destroyed most of the volcanic island and generated deadly tsunamis.

title: Last spike of the Canadian Pacific Railway
note: Donald Smith drove the last spike at Craigellachie, completing Canada's first transcontinental railway.

title: First Zionist Congress opens in Basel
note: Theodor Herzl convened the congress that adopted the Basel Program calling for a Jewish home in the Land of Israel.

title: Gideons organized in Janesville
note: Three Christian commercial travelers formally organized the association later known for placing Bibles in hotels.

title: Agnes Ozman speaks in tongues at Topeka
note: At Charles Parham's Bethel Bible College, Ozman's experience became a starting point of modern Pentecostalism.

title: Marconi receives first transatlantic radio signal
note: At Signal Hill, St. John's, Marconi reported hearing the Morse letter S sent from Poldhu, Cornwall.

title: Wright brothers' first powered flight
note: Orville and Wilbur Wright made the first controlled, sustained powered airplane flights at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.

title: Evan Roberts' first revival meeting at Loughor
note: A small meeting of young people at Moriah chapel is generally regarded as the start of the 1904-05 Welsh Revival.

title: Bloody Sunday in St Petersburg
note: Troops fired on a peaceful procession of workers petitioning the tsar, sparking the 1905 Revolution (9 January Old Style).

title: Revival begins at Bonnie Brae Street, Los Angeles
note: Prayer meetings led by William J. Seymour broke out in tongues and soon moved to 312 Azusa Street, launching the Azusa Street Revival.

title: San Francisco earthquake
note: A major earthquake and the fires that followed destroyed much of San Francisco.

title: Silver Dart makes Canada's first powered flight
note: J.A.D. McCurdy flew the Aerial Experiment Association's Silver Dart over the ice of Bras d'Or Lake at Baddeck.

title: World Missionary Conference opens in Edinburgh
note: The gathering of Protestant mission societies is often seen as the starting point of the modern ecumenical movement.

title: RMS Titanic sinks
note: The liner sank after striking an iceberg; many of the recovered victims were brought to Halifax and buried there.

title: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
note: Gavrilo Princip shot the heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne in Sarajevo, setting off the crisis that led to the First World War.

title: Britain declares war on Germany
note: Britain's declaration brought Canada and the rest of the Empire into the First World War.

title: Tsar Nicholas II abdicates
note: During the February Revolution the tsar signed his abdication at Pskov, ending Romanov rule (2 March Old Style).

title: Battle of Vimy Ridge begins
note: All four divisions of the Canadian Corps attacked together and captured the ridge over the following days.

title: Balfour Declaration
note: Foreign Secretary Arthur Balfour's letter to Lord Rothschild stated British support for a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine.

title: October Revolution in Petrograd
note: The Bolsheviks seized power from the Provisional Government; the Winter Palace fell overnight (25 October Old Style).

title: Halifax Explosion
note: The munitions ship Mont-Blanc collided with the Imo in the Narrows and exploded, killing about 2,000 people and devastating north-end Halifax.

title: General Allenby enters Jerusalem
note: The British commander entered the Old City on foot through the Jaffa Gate after Ottoman forces withdrew.

title: Armistice ends fighting in the First World War
note: The armistice signed at Compiègne took effect at 11 a.m., ending hostilities on the Western Front.

title: Treaty of Versailles signed
note: The peace treaty between Germany and the Allied powers was signed in the Hall of Mirrors.

title: Schooner Bluenose launched at Lunenburg
note: The fishing and racing schooner built by Smith and Rhuland went on to become an emblem of Nova Scotia.

title: United Church of Canada inaugurated
note: Methodists, Congregationalists and most Presbyterians united at a service in Toronto's Mutual Street Arena.

title: Pier 21 opens in Halifax
note: The ocean immigration shed opened; about a million immigrants, refugees and war brides later entered Canada through it.

title: Black Tuesday stock market crash
note: Panic selling on the New York Stock Exchange marked the deepest day of the 1929 crash and the onset of the Great Depression.

title: Barmen Theological Declaration adopted
note: The Confessing Synod at Barmen affirmed the sole lordship of Christ over the church against state-imposed ideology.

title: Kristallnacht pogrom
note: Over the night of 9-10 November, synagogues, Jewish homes and businesses across Germany and Austria were attacked.

title: Germany invades Poland
note: The German invasion began the Second World War in Europe.

title: Canada declares war on Germany
note: In its first independent declaration of war, Canada entered the Second World War a week after Britain.

title: Attack on Pearl Harbor
note: Japanese aircraft attacked the US Pacific Fleet in Hawaii, bringing the United States into the war.

title: Wannsee Conference
note: Senior Nazi officials met near Berlin to coordinate the deportation and murder of Europe's Jews.

title: D-Day landings in Normandy
note: Allied forces, including Canadians at Juno Beach, landed in Normandy to open a western front.

title: Liberation of Auschwitz
note: Soviet troops reached the Auschwitz camp complex; the date is now International Holocaust Remembrance Day.

title: Dietrich Bonhoeffer executed
note: The Lutheran pastor and theologian, an opponent of the Nazi regime, was hanged at Flossenbürg concentration camp.

title: Victory in Europe Day
note: The Allies formally accepted Germany's unconditional surrender, ending the war in Europe.

title: Atomic bombing of Hiroshima
note: A US aircraft dropped the first atomic bomb used in war on Hiroshima.

title: United Nations Charter enters into force
note: The UN came into existence once the Charter had been ratified by the required states; the date is marked as UN Day.

title: Viola Desmond refuses to leave a whites-only section
note: The Halifax businesswoman was arrested at New Glasgow's Roseland Theatre, a landmark in Canadian civil rights history.

title: India and Pakistan become independent
note: British rule ended and India became independent, a day after Pakistan's creation, amid the partition of the subcontinent.

title: UN adopts the Partition Plan for Palestine
note: General Assembly Resolution 181 recommended dividing Mandatory Palestine into Jewish and Arab states with an international Jerusalem.

title: Israel's Declaration of Independence
note: David Ben-Gurion proclaimed the State of Israel in Tel Aviv as the British Mandate ended.

title: World Council of Churches founded
note: The WCC was formally constituted at its first assembly in Amsterdam.

title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights adopted
note: The UN General Assembly in Paris adopted the declaration, drafted with Canadian John Humphrey's involvement.

title: Newfoundland joins Canada
note: Newfoundland became Canada's tenth province just before midnight on 31 March.

title: Billy Graham's Los Angeles campaign begins
note: The eight-week tent campaign brought Graham to national prominence.

title: Five missionaries killed in Ecuador
note: Jim Elliot, Nate Saint and three colleagues were killed by Waorani men; family members later lived among the Waorani.

title: Sputnik 1 launched
note: The Soviet Union put the first artificial satellite into orbit.

title: Springhill mining disaster
note: An underground 'bump' in the Springhill coal mine killed 75 miners; others were rescued after days underground.

title: Adolf Eichmann captured in Buenos Aires
note: Israeli agents seized the Holocaust organizer, who was later tried and executed in Israel.

title: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space
note: Gagarin orbited Earth once aboard Vostok 1.

title: Construction of the Berlin Wall begins
note: East German authorities sealed the border between East and West Berlin overnight.

title: Second Vatican Council opens
note: Pope John XXIII opened the council that reshaped Catholic liturgy and relations with other churches.

title: President John F. Kennedy assassinated
note: Kennedy was shot and killed in a motorcade in Dallas, Texas.

title: Maple Leaf flag first raised
note: The new National Flag of Canada was officially inaugurated on Parliament Hill.

title: Israeli paratroopers reach the Temple Mount
note: During the Six-Day War, Israeli forces took the Old City; commander Motta Gur radioed "The Temple Mount is in our hands."

title: Apollo 11 lands on the Moon
note: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first humans to land on the Moon.

title: Lausanne Congress on World Evangelization opens
note: Some 2,700 evangelical leaders gathered and produced the Lausanne Covenant.

title: Entebbe raid
note: Israeli commandos rescued hostages from a hijacked airliner at Entebbe airport.

title: Camp David Accords signed
note: Egypt's Sadat and Israel's Begin signed frameworks for peace brokered by Jimmy Carter.

title: Constitution Act, 1982 proclaimed
note: Queen Elizabeth II proclaimed the patriated constitution, including the Charter of Rights and Freedoms, in Ottawa.

title: Chernobyl nuclear disaster
note: Reactor No. 4 at the Chernobyl plant exploded, releasing radioactive material across Europe.

title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
note: East Germany opened its border crossings, and crowds began crossing and dismantling the Wall.

title: Operation Solomon airlifts Ethiopian Jews
note: In about 36 hours over 24-25 May, Israel flew some 14,000 Ethiopian Jews from Addis Ababa to Israel.

title: Soviet Union formally dissolved
note: The Supreme Soviet's upper chamber voted the USSR out of existence, a day after Gorbachev resigned.

title: Westray Mine explosion
note: A methane and coal-dust explosion at Plymouth, Pictou County, killed all 26 miners underground.

title: Oslo I Accord signed
note: Israel and the PLO signed the Declaration of Principles at the White House.

title: Toronto Airport Vineyard revival begins
note: Meetings with Randy Clark began a long-running charismatic revival known as the Toronto Blessing.

title: Nelson Mandela inaugurated president
note: Mandela became South Africa's first president elected in a fully representative democratic election.

title: Swissair Flight 111 crashes off Peggy's Cove
note: The MD-11 crashed into St. Margarets Bay after an in-flight fire, killing all 229 aboard.

title: Catholic-Lutheran Joint Declaration on Justification
note: The Lutheran World Federation and the Catholic Church signed a common statement on justification in Augsburg.

title: September 11 attacks
note: Hijacked airliners struck the World Trade Center and Pentagon; diverted flights landed in Gander and Halifax.

title: Hurricane Juan strikes Halifax
note: Juan made landfall near Halifax as a Category 2 hurricane, causing deaths and widespread damage.

title: Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami
note: A magnitude 9.1 earthquake off Sumatra generated tsunamis that killed about 230,000 people in many countries.

title: Pope John Paul II dies
note: The Polish-born pope died after a pontificate of more than 26 years.

title: Apple announces the iPhone
note: Steve Jobs unveiled the iPhone, which helped define the smartphone era.

title: Tohoku earthquake, tsunami and Fukushima accident
note: A magnitude 9.0 earthquake and tsunami killed nearly 20,000 people and triggered the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear accident.

title: CERN announces Higgs boson discovery
note: The ATLAS and CMS experiments reported observing a new particle consistent with the Higgs boson.

title: Pope Benedict XVI's resignation takes effect
note: Benedict became the first pope in nearly six centuries to resign.

title: WHO declares COVID-19 a pandemic
note: The World Health Organization characterized the COVID-19 outbreak as a pandemic.

title: Abraham Accords signed
note: Israel, the UAE and Bahrain signed normalization agreements at the White House.

title: James Webb Space Telescope launched
note: An Ariane 5 rocket launched the telescope, built by NASA with ESA and the Canadian Space Agency.

title: Russia launches full-scale invasion of Ukraine
note: Russian forces invaded Ukraine on several fronts, beginning Europe's largest war since 1945.

title: Queen Elizabeth II dies
note: The Queen of the United Kingdom and Canada died at Balmoral after a 70-year reign; Charles III succeeded her.

title: Post-tropical storm Fiona hits Nova Scotia
note: Fiona made landfall in eastern Nova Scotia, causing record low pressure and severe damage across Atlantic Canada.

title: Asbury revival begins
note: A routine chapel service at Asbury University in Kentucky continued for about two weeks of round-the-clock worship.

title: Hamas-led attack on Israel
note: Militants from Gaza killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel and took some 250 hostages, starting the Gaza war.

title: Notre-Dame de Paris reopens
note: The cathedral reopened with a ceremony five years after the 2019 fire.

title: Fall of the Assad government in Syria
note: Opposition forces entered Damascus and Bashar al-Assad fled the country.

title: Mark Carney sworn in as prime minister
note: Carney succeeded Justin Trudeau as Canada's 24th prime minister.

title: Pope Francis dies
note: The first Latin American pope died on Easter Monday at age 88.

title: Pope Leo XIV elected
note: Cardinal Robert Prevost was elected as the first pope from the United States.

title: Israel strikes Iran, beginning a twelve-day war
note: Israel attacked Iranian nuclear and military sites; a ceasefire took effect on 24 June.

title: Last living Israeli hostages released from Gaza
note: Under a ceasefire deal, Hamas freed the remaining 20 living hostages and Israel released Palestinian prisoners.

title: US strikes Venezuela and captures Maduro
note: US forces carried out strikes in Venezuela and took Nicolás Maduro into custody to face charges in New York.

title: Milano Cortina Winter Olympics open
note: The XXV Olympic Winter Games opened with a ceremony at Milan's San Siro stadium.

title: Ayatollah Khamenei killed in US-Israeli strikes
note: Iran's supreme leader was killed in strikes on the first day of a US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

title: Artemis II launches crew around the Moon
note: NASA launched four astronauts, including Canadian Jeremy Hansen, on the first crewed lunar mission since 1972; they splashed down on 10 April.

title: Twin earthquakes strike Venezuela
note: Two major earthquakes caused thousands of deaths and widespread destruction.

title: Spain wins the 2026 FIFA World Cup
note: Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in the final of the first World Cup co-hosted by Canada, Mexico and the United States.
